_about: Italian East Africa and the Sahara posts, June 1940 to December 1941: the garrisons the far chart did not have (the design director's ruling C of 11:40Z and his acceptance of 13:09Z, 22 November 2026, on the historian's iea-sahara-1940-41.md, sources E1 to E30). Until these rows East Africa stood empty on the far chart, Britain's Sudan, Kenya and Somaliland too, and the fronts there read hundreds to one. Laid as data, as found, behind the far switch (far-rows.ts lays this file last); nothing is fitted to a result. Written by /mnt/project-files/pacific-six/far-africa-make.py and kept by hand after.
_form: A row is the chart's dated row: month, nation, formation, kind, divisions, place, words. 'est' is the row's size by date as a share of its divisions (worth = divisions x est), the record's men at 15,000 to 1.0. 'until' with 'holds' is the row's last month: at the book's stops the row ends in that month by date; where the book is not kept it stands while its place is held and ends when it is lost (game.ts, lentOver). 'ends': 'surrender' gives the card a surrender's words where a lent row's would say it left for other fronts. 'mark' is the historian's mark where it is not F: L likely, D derived, U uncertain; 'memory' is a row from memory, which no card prints until it is checked.
_italy: Italy's army on 1 June 1940 by its six commands and the headquarters, 17.1 (255,950 men, [E6]): headquarters 0.5, Eritrea 2.8, Amhara 4.0, Shoa 3.6, Galla-Sidamo 2.1, Harar 2.5, Somalia 1.6. The pages give the commands and their seats, not their borders: each command's worth is shared evenly over the far-side places the file lists as its ground, so that each place has its holder and its own last month (D, the builder's arithmetic). All forces from 1 August 1940, 24.7 (371,053 men): each row grows in the same share from month 12 (D). From month 21 the file's 'over 80,000 in the field': Gondar 2.7 and Galla-Sidamo 2.5, the latter shared evenly by Jimma and Lekemti (D); Assab from 21 at the 582 men taken there, 0.04 (D). From 23 Gondar alone, 2.7.
_months: Each place's last Italian month is the file's table by far-side province: Mogadishu and Kismayu 18; Neghelli, Harar and Keren 19; Asmara, Debra Markos, Addis Ababa, Massawa and Dessie 20; Assab and Jimma 22; Gondar 27. Kufra 19. The places the pages do not date stand at the file's derived months with their marks: Belet Uen, Gabredarre (D), Obbia and Bender Cassim (U) at 19, the later month of '18 or 19', since they lie behind Mogadishu (25 February) on the road north; Mekele 21 and Lekemti 23, 'at the latest'. Where two pages disagree inside a month the month stands (Massawa, Dessie, Mega, Agibar, Wolchefit); Jimma 22 by Playfair, the firmer page.
_notLaid: Not laid, for the design director's word: (1) the gains of July and August 1940 (Kassala 11 to 17, Hargeisa and Berbera 12 to 19). The Kassala force and Nasi's force were brigades of the commands above, not more men, and the pages give Nasi's force no men: no row is added for them, and no dated attack is laid, so Italy's staff takes those places or does not. (2) The 4th Indian Division's loan from Egypt (17 to 20): it is the desert's own corps on the old chart; a dated row would re-form it without its record and nothing would bring it back. (3) The South Africans in Kenya (the 1st South African Division, 1.8, and the 2nd Brigade at Berbera): South Africa is a seat with its own army on this chart, and the desert's old row brings the 1st South African Division to Egypt in month 21. (4) The 23rd Nigerian and 24th Gold Coast Brigades: the pages give no men, and they stood inside the two African divisions. (5) Sebha and Waw el Kebir: the record is silent. The Fezzan's rows have no last month: it stays Italian past 28. (6) Vichy's Djibouti after December 1941 (it ended in month 40) is beyond the file's months.
_facing: The forces facing Italy as the file lists them. The Sudan: the Sudan Defence Force 0.3 at Kassala; the three British battalions, 0.3 (all troops 0.6 less the Defence Force, D), which the 5th Indian Division takes in when it comes in month 13 (worth 1, D: the chart's own unit for a division with no men given, replaced when sourced), lent until 22; Gideon Force 0.1 from 17 to 21, posted to Debra Markos, and the Brigade d'Orient 0.1 (U) from 18 to 21 at Port Sudan, where it landed. Both are Britain's rows on this chart: the Free French have no flag of their own after France falls. Kenya: the King's African Rifles 1.5; the 11th African Division (1, D) at Garissa from 11 to 27 and the 12th (1, D) at Wajir from 11: 3.5 together beside the file's 3.2 for Kenya's troops other than South Africa's at the end of November 1940. Somaliland: Chater's force 0.1, taken off in month 12 (its 0.3 of early August never stood a whole month); the Aden Striking Force 0.2 from 19, posted to Berbera. The Belgian Congo's expedition, 0.15 (the middle of 0.1 to 0.2), from 19 to 23 at Gambela, the place the file's own text has it take in March 1941: Britain's row, since Belgium has fallen and Lekemti, the file's place, is Italy's. Djibouti: the garrison, 1.0 in June 1940 and 0.5 from July, raised in the place ('levy'), so it goes with Djibouti's keeper when France falls. Chad: Leclerc's troops 0.2 from month 12 at Fort-Lamy, a memory row (U). The five garrisons the file has standing on 10 June 1940 (the Defence Force, the British battalions, the King's African Rifles, Chater's force and Djibouti's garrison) are laid in month 9: the file's tables begin at 10, the month Italy came into the war, and on this chart Italy's month comes before Britain's and France's, so a row of month 10 would not stand on the day Italy's war opened (D).
